result: Narrowed; original status retained. For every assignment of Boolean edge signs to a triangle and every Boolean vertex switching, the XOR of the three edge signs is invariant. A switching makes all three edge signs positive exactly when their XOR is zero. An explicit switching gives the normal form (0,0,parity), and the product of integer edge signs equals the sign of that parity. A negative-parity triangle is obstructed within this switching class, whereas a balanced triangle with two negative edges can be made positive.
proof_boundary: Only diagonal vertex-sign switching on one three-cycle is classified. No spin bordism group, eta invariant, fermion representation, bulk cancellation or obstruction over all representations is computed. The original cobordism-based intrinsic-sign claim remains open.
